audit.why: EVEN / 6/10 fits 51.03% over 876 games. Gnar owns the ranged laning phase against a dashless Sion; Sion earns the even back with tank items and Glory in Death.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with the page's own whys, and the packet agrees with the whys in every one. whys[0] says neither owns level 1 (stored Gnar), whys[1] says Gnar punishes for free (stored Skill), whys[2] says Gnar kites a Sion who cannot close (stored Sion), whys[3] calls it a coinflip (stored Sion), whys[4] says 'call it skill' (stored Gnar), whys[5] says the tempo pulls Gnar's way (stored Sion). Separately whys[3] and whys[4] are shifted a slot — whys[3] sits on Levels 4-5 but opens 'It's a coinflip at 6', and whys[4] sits on Level 6 but says neither side spikes, ignoring Unstoppable Onslaught entirely.
audit.why: Sion's level-6 spike is a 140-second map-wide charge whose knockup scales with charge distance; leaving it off the level-6 row was the largest omission on the page.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped to Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Sion as one atomic group across both layers, whys[3] re-anchored to Levels 4-5 and whys[4] rewritten around Unstoppable Onslaught.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) The early block says his E 'shield-breaks back' — Roar of the Slayer does nothing of the kind. It is an 800-range shockwave that damages, slows and REDUCES ARMOUR, and knocks a struck minion backwards through everything behind it. (b) Soul Furnace is described only as a shield; the page never says it re-activates after three seconds to deal magic damage to everyone nearby, which is what actually punishes a Gnar who stands next to a freshly shielded Sion.
audit.why: The invented shield-break sends the reader looking for an interaction that does not exist, and the armour shred plus the W detonation are the two facts that decide extended trades. The armour shred is also the flagged resistances-invalidated gap: Plated Steelcaps is not the answer to him.
audit.corrected: Roar of the Slayer (E, 12/11/10/9/8s, 800 range) slows and shreds armour, and knocks minions back through you. Soul Furnace (W, 15/14/13/12/11s) shields and re-fires after three seconds for magic damage. Decimating Smash (Q, 10s at rank 1) only knocks up when fully charged. Unstoppable Onslaught (R, 140/100/60s) knocks up harder the further it charges. Glory in Death heals him, so Grievous Wounds timing decides post-death fights.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Sion carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two tank items in, his HP and armour shrug off Mega burst and his zombie fights on — stop soloing him, engage for the team.

edits.before: It's a coinflip at 6: strong if Rage lines up for a Mega Wallop stun, but a liability if Gnar's stuck in Mini when the charged Decimating Smash knockup lands.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a coinflip: strong when Rage lines up for a Mega Wallop stun, a liability in Mini when a charged Decimating Smash knockup lands.

edits.before: Neither gets a true power spike here — it comes down to whether Mega is up; with it Gnar wall-combos for a kill, with Sion just farming it's a wash, so call it skill.
edits.after: At 6 he gets Unstoppable Onslaught on 140 seconds, a map-wide charge whose knockup scales with distance; with Mega up you answer it, without it you do not.

edits.before: Sion can't catch you, so this is a free poke lane in Mini — auto-and-Boomerang his big base HP and step out before his E (Roar of the Slayer) shield-breaks back. The one thing that flips it is a fully-charged Decimating Smash: never stand still when he's winding up the Q, and especially don't get knocked up while your Rage bar is mid-transition between forms. At level 2 his lack of a dash means Hyper's third-hit proc and its move-speed burst let you walk in, chunk him, and walk out for nothing.
edits.after: Sion can't catch you, so this is a free poke lane in Mini — auto-and-Boomerang his big base HP and step out before Roar of the Slayer (E, 800 range) answers: it slows and shreds your armour, so stacking plates is not the fix here. The one thing that flips it is a fully-charged Decimating Smash: never stand still while he winds up the Q, and never eat that knockup mid-transform. At level 2 his lack of a dash means Hyper's third-hit proc and its move-speed burst let you walk in, chunk him, and walk out for free.

edits.before: Keep abusing the range gap — he shields your poke with Soul Furnace, but that's mana and a cooldown he'd rather spend last-hitting, so chip him while he's stuck reacting. The volatile part is Rage RNG: if you're in Mini at zero Rage when he charges Q, that knockup plus E poke is a real chunk, so respect his Q timer like any cooldown. When Mega is up you can Wallop-stun him or use GNAR! into a wall for a kill, but he's tanky and a whiffed combo gives him a free trade back, so only commit when the Rage lines up.
edits.after: Keep abusing the range gap — Soul Furnace (W, 15s at rank 1) eats your poke, but it re-activates three seconds later for magic damage, so chip him and step back instead of standing beside a fresh shield. The volatile part is Rage RNG: in Mini at zero Rage when he charges Q (10s at rank 1), that knockup plus E poke is a real chunk. With Mega up you Wallop-stun him or GNAR! him into a wall, but he is tanky and a whiffed combo hands him a free trade back, so commit only when the Rage lines up.

edits.before: Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Fully charged Q knocks up; it is 10s at rank 1 and travels far.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.

notes: Fabricated mechanic removed: Sion's E was described as shield-breaking. It shreds armour instead, which also resolves the flagged resistances-invalidated gap — Plated Steelcaps is the wrong first answer into him. The packet's suspect name 'Soul Furnace's' is a false positive (possessive form of the real name). Whether Unstoppable Onslaught can be interrupted by Gnar's Wallop or GNAR! is the one thing I could not verify from the kit — Riot's text says nothing about crowd-control immunity during the charge, so I wrote no claim either way; see unverified. The content whys are written in the third person ('Gnar's Mini kit', 'Gnar wall-combos') rather than the user's second-person voice; I only converted the lines I was already editing, since the rest have no factual error and voice-only rewrites would spend the length band for nothing.
